circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the venue for Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009 and was designed by Hermann Tilke. As the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be built, it followed Bahrain's establishment and preceded later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix, along with Supercars and additional support categories. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally built as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following reconstruction and renaming in the 1990s, it resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix for another seven-year period in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track positioned along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, spanning 6. 003 km per lap to rank as the fourth-lengthiest venue on the F1 calendar. The circuit first hosted F1 racing in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix staged in the Middle East. Beyond its primary F1 role, the facility accommodates diverse racing categories including drag racing, GP2 Series events, and 24-hour endurance competitions, holding a FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Montmeló near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One machinery. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Francorchamps circuit near Spa, Belgium spans 7. 004 kilometres and stands as one of motor racing's most historic venues, having hosted Grand Prix racing since 1925 and featured in the inaugural Formula One season of 1950. The track has continuously staged the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361 km circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix and has previously accommodated various international racing series including World Sportscar Championship events and multiple NASCAR competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has been China's primary Formula One venue, hosting the Chinese Grand Prix intermittently since 2004 with a break between 2020 and 2023 before resuming in 2024. Beyond its marquee F1 event, the facility has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing series starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing circuit located near the Northamptonshire hamlets of Silverstone and Whittlebury that has been the principal venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948. The track gained further significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the British Grand Prix later alternated between three circuits from 1955 until returning exclusively to Silverstone in 1987. Beyond Formula One, the venue also stages the British round of motorcycle racing's premier series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other F1 venue, the track was constructed outside the city after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. The venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, missing only the 1980 season during renovations, and remains one of Formula One's most historic and consistent fixtures.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, operated by Honda Mobilityland in Japan's Mie Prefecture, is a 5. 807 km track renowned as a Formula One grand prix venue alongside the Japanese Super Formula series. The facility holds 155,000 spectators and ranks among motorsport's most prestigious racing destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following portions of the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where the city's premier resorts and entertainment venues are located. The 3. 8-kilometer layout passes iconic destinations such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it weaves through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both accomplished racing drivers who died in separate on-track incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during three distinct eras, with the current arrangement beginning in 2015 following a 23-year absence, now officially known as the Mexico City Grand Prix.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners designed by specialist track architects. The venue joined the Formula One calendar in 2022, hosting the Miami Grand Prix with average qualifying speeds near 139 mph, and has since accommodated Formula E racing on an adapted configuration beginning in 2025.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbour area. Though technically named for the principality itself, the circuit is widely known as "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 to 2026. The venue earned its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname from its distinctive combination of steeply banked corners and dramatic elevation changes winding through the seaside landscape.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometer track featuring a notably long 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 status.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later dedicated to Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace following his 1977 death. The counterclockwise track has hosted numerous grands prix and features an adjacent kart facility honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since 2021, it has served as the permanent home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and recently began hosting Formula E competition from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang areas, utilizing public roads that border Marina Bay as its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA track that serves as the venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside other major motorsport competitions including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship. Beyond Formula One, the facility has hosted various racing series over the years, ranging from IndyCar to sports car championships and international rallycross events.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a driver holding both Thai and British nationality, currently races for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso represents Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two world championship titles from his 2005-2006 Renault years alongside 32 career Grand Prix victories accumulated over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to claim both Formula One and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli claimed the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes, setting the record as the sport's youngest champion, having secured nine race victories following his series entry in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently drives for Haas in Formula One competition.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto is a Brazilian motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the sport. He achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during consecutive years at Mercedes before securing 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian racing driver competing in the Asian Le Mans Series LMP2 category with AF Corse, following his previous involvement with Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series. In Formula One, he has served as a reserve driver for Haas and made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved a career-defining victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver representing France in Formula One, currently races for Red Bull Racing. He holds dual French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having established himself as one of the sport's most decorated competitors with seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds numerous performance records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing experience from a successful career in endurance motorsport that included a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine career victories over nine seasons. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, nicknamed K-Mag, has split his racing career between Formula One stints spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, and currently campaigns in the FIA World Endurance Championship representing BMW through the WRT team as a factory driver.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while accumulating 14 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, recently drove for Haas in Formula One after previously securing a Grand Prix victory with Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as runner-up in the 2023 drivers' championship while at Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories during his tenure across four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One across 14 seasons from 2011 until 2024, claiming victory in eight Grand Prix events during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Mercedes who has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories over the course of his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant, an American driver, raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to the FIA World Endurance Championship. He is currently preparing to compete for Ford in the series, having previously driven in the LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat for five consecutive seasons beginning in 2021 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch driver Max Verstappen has dominated Formula One in recent years, claiming four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing. Over 12 seasons, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories, establishing himself as one of the sport's most successful drivers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a Formula One driver, currently holding a reserve position with Cadillac. The Beijing-born competitor actively raced in the series across 2022 and 2024, establishing himself as the sole Chinese national to participate in Formula One's highest level.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team rebranded as Alpine for the 2021 season to represent Renault's sports car division while continuing as the manufacturer's official works outfit. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025, the team's long association with the French automotive group came to an end.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One across multiple eras under different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited and racing under the Aston Martin designation in the championship.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, is the sport's most decorated and enduring team, participating continuously in Formula One championships since the competition's inaugural 1950 season. Renowned by the nickname "the Prancing Horse" after their distinctive emblem, the squad has established itself as both the longest-standing and most accomplished outfit in the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American racing entrepreneur Gene Haas founded this Formula One team in 2014, debuting on the grid in 2016 with American licensing. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed leadership as team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss motorsport engineering firm founded in 1970 that excelled in endurance racing, notably winning the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours, before establishing itself as a Formula One constructor from 1993 onwards. The team competed independently through numerous iterations until Audi acquired its operations and assets in 2024, marking the end of its 32-year tenure in the sport as one of the grid's longest-standing independent constructors.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited operates as a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility in Surrey. The team functions as part of the broader McLaren Group, which is entirely owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in 2022. Mercedes teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team portfolio. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team to Red Bull Racing while maintaining its own constructor status.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as a sister team to Red Bull Racing under Red Bull GmbH ownership. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as one of two Red Bull-owned constructors on the grid.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, has been a Formula One competitor since 2005 and currently operates as Oracle Red Bull Racing. The team, owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Racing Bulls, was led by Christian Horner from its inception until 2025, when Laurent Mekies assumed the role of team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. The team maintains its headquarters at a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, where it has developed and competed with its own chassis since its inception.
